Issued at 301 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

===== Thanksgiving Evening - Friday =====

It is a dreary and waterlogged Thanksgiving across the area, with 
radar mosaic showing bands of light to moderate rain pivoting from 
south to north. Temperatures are in the mid-40s for most, so no 
concern for any snow mixing in due to these mild temps for the 
afternoon. Per the KY Mesonet, we have already picked up roughly 1.0-
1.5" of rainfall in the last 24 hours. We've been able to handle 
this steady rain due to the ongoing drought conditions across the 
region, and with relatively high flash flood guidance. This 
Thanksgiving has already been one for the record books in Lexington, 
becoming the wettest Thanksgiving on record there. As of 3pm EST, 
they have received 1.35" of rain, with more on the way this evening 
and tonight. 

On a synoptic view, the upper low is centered over western TN this 
afternoon, with the associated vort max located across northern AL. 
With the sfc low off to our east, an unusual placement of the 
easterly LLJ remains to our north, and an inverted sfc trough 
sitting along the I-64 corridor. Though PWATs have dropped below 1 
inch as the moisture advection has weakened, still expect 
additional light rain or drizzle through tonight as the upper low 
spins overhead. 

Favorable critical thicknesses have remain confined to far western 
KY and into middle TN this afternoon, which has resulted in some 
snowfall to our west and south. We'll stick with the rain through 
the afternoon and most of the evening, but there is a chance for 
some snow mixing in with the rain for a small area by late tonight. 
The best chance for that happening will be along a line stretching 
from Tompkinsville to Russell Springs to Berea, where more favorable 
critical thicknesses to support snow will be overnight. The Lake 
Cumberland area also has the best chance for temps dropping to near 
freezing tonight. No snow accumulations are expected, and chances 
for 0.01" of snow has dropped from 15% to nearly 0% with today's new 
data. We'll continue to mention a rain-snow mix in our southeast, 
but don't have any expectations for impacts there overnight. By 
tomorrow morning, that chance for some light snow mixing in with 
rain could switch over to portions of southern IN with the colder 
temps finally arriving. Madison, IN could see some flakes mixed in 
with the rain, but chances for snow accumulations are less than 10%. 
Additional rainfall of 0.50-1.0" is expected through tomorrow 
morning.

Precip chances will eventually exit from west to east during the day 
tomorrow. Those chances will linger later in the day for the 
Bluegrass, which could see some light rain until around sunset 
tomorrow. Highs for tomorrow will only be in the low 40s again, so a 
similar forecast to today but will lighter rainfall. 


===== Weekend Forecast =====

The upper flow regime flattens out into zonal flow by Saturday, with 
a sfc high located near New Orleans. Sfc ridging will extend 
northward from that high pressure zone, and will extend far enough 
north into the Ohio Valley. We'll see some sunshine return, along 
with temp in the 50s, making for a nice late-November day. 

Our next rain chances will arrive Sunday morning as an upper 
shortwave trough moves across the central US, pushing a sfc low 
through the mid-Mississippi Valley. Model soundings are not 
supportive for instability, so mainly a higher shear environment 
with the sfc low passing through. Expect mostly rain showers, but a 
few thunderstorms could be possible during the day. QPF amounts 
around half an inch are most likely with 60-70%, and around a 25-30% 
chance for more than an inch. 

===== Next Week =====

Zonal flow returns for next week, and sfc high pressure filtering 
into the area. This will lead to a dry start to next week, with 
daily highs slightly warmer each day. Monday will be in the upper 
40s and near 50, but we'll be closer to 60 by Wednesday. Precip 
chances may return by Thursday of next week.
